english.title: Make off when required to wait with a secure college custody officer
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been required, under paragraph 11(2) of Schedule 10 to the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015, to wait with **(..SPECIFY SECURE COLLEGE CUSTODY OFFICER..), a secure college custody officer performing custodial duties at a contracted-out secure college, namely **(..SPECIFY SECURE COLLEGE..), for the arrival of a constable for such period as was necessary, made off during that period
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 11(4) of Schedule 10 to the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015.

english.notes:
(i) A secure college custody officer performing custodial duties at a contracted-out secure college may exercise the powers granted by paragraph 11(2) if he has reason to believe that a person who is in the college or seeking to enter the college, other than a person detained there, is committing or has committed an offence under any of sections 39 to 40D of the Prison Act 1952 (this includes attempting or conspiring to commit such an offence or encouraging or assisting the offence).
(ii) A secure college custody officer may require the person to wait with the officer for the arrival of a constable for such period as is necessary, except that the person may not be required to wait for longer than 2 hours
(iii) A secure college custody officer may use reasonable force to prevent the person from making off during that period
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, having been required, under paragraph 11(2) of Schedule 10 to the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015, to wait with **(..SPECIFY SECURE COLLEGE CUSTODY OFFICER..), a secure college custody officer performing custodial duties at a contracted-out secure college, namely **(..SPECIFY SECURE COLLEGE..), for the arrival of a constable for such period as was necessary, made off during that period.
